title: The Play Without a Single Stage
title_ja: 一つの舞台を持たない演劇
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: An imaginary theater company plans a performance in which the audience moves between several small rooms.
sentences.ja: 架空の劇団は観客が複数の小部屋を移動する公演を企画する。

sentences.en: Each room contains a scene that reveals a different character's experience of the same fictional event.
sentences.ja: 各部屋には同じ架空の出来事について異なる登場人物の経験を示す場面がある。

sentences.en: Because participants are unable to visit every room simultaneously, they encounter the scenes in different sequences.
sentences.ja: 全室を同時に訪れられないため異なる順序で場面に出会う。

sentences.en: The director hopes that these variations will encourage people to reconsider how they construct an understanding of a story.
sentences.ja: 違いが物語の理解の構築方法を再考するよう促すことを演出家は期待する。

sentences.en: During rehearsals, one actor worries that certain spectators might leave without encountering information essential to interpreting the ending.
sentences.ja: 練習中、ある俳優は結末の解釈に不可欠な情報に触れず帰る観客を心配する。

sentences.en: Another argues that missing information is an intentional feature of the performance rather than a problem that should automatically be eliminated.
sentences.ja: 情報の欠落は自動的に除くべき問題でなく意図した特徴だと別の俳優は主張する。

sentences.en: The company distinguishes between uncertainty that invites meaningful reflection and confusion that prevents an audience from engaging with the work.
sentences.ja: 意味ある考察を促す不確実性と作品に関わることを妨げる混乱を区別する。

sentences.en: They recognize that the same artistic decision might produce either experience depending on the context in which it occurs.
sentences.ja: 同じ芸術的判断も状況によりどちらの体験も生み得ると認識する。

sentences.en: The director prepares several imaginary audience routes and examines which events can be understood without seeing every scene.
sentences.ja: 複数の架空観客経路を用意し全場面を見なくても理解できる出来事を検討する。

sentences.en: She introduces recurring objects and phrases that connect separate rooms without explaining every relationship explicitly.
sentences.ja: 全関係を明示せず別室を結ぶ繰り返し現れる物や言葉を導入する。

sentences.en: The company also provides clear instructions about movement through the building so that practical uncertainty does not interfere unnecessarily with the artistic experience.
sentences.ja: 実務的な不確かさが芸術体験を不必要に妨げないよう建物内移動の明確な指示も提供する。

sentences.en: The revised design therefore preserves differences in interpretation while reducing difficulties unrelated to the story.
sentences.ja: 修正版は物語と無関係な困難を減らしつつ解釈の違いを維持する。

sentences.en: At the end of the performance, the audience is invited to discuss the scenes that different participants encountered.
sentences.ja: 終演後観客は異なる参加者が出会った場面を話し合うよう招かれる。

sentences.en: Some discover that an apparently unimportant action had considerable significance from another character's perspective.
sentences.ja: 一見重要でない行為が別の登場人物の視点ではかなり重要だったと知る人もいる。

sentences.en: Others realize that knowing additional information does not always settle disagreements about the characters' intentions.
sentences.ja: 追加情報が分かっても登場人物の意図についての不一致が必ず解決するわけではないと気づく人もいる。

sentences.en: The discussion becomes another part of the artistic experience rather than a test with one officially correct interpretation.
sentences.ja: 議論は公式の正解一つを持つ試験でなく芸術体験の別の一部となる。

sentences.en: The fictional performance illustrates that the order in which information is encountered can influence the meaning people initially assign to it.
sentences.ja: 架空公演は情報に触れる順序が最初に与える意味に影響し得ると示す。

sentences.en: An artistic work can deliberately make this process visible by allowing its audience to encounter different aspects of the same event.
sentences.ja: 芸術作品は同じ出来事の異なる側面に触れさせることでこの過程を意図的に見えるようにできる。

sentences.en: Such a design requires attention to the distinction between productive ambiguity and unnecessary obstacles to participation.
sentences.ja: こうした設計には有益な曖昧さと不要な参加障壁の区別への注意が必要だ。

sentences.en: For this theater company, variation is not a failure to reproduce an identical performance but an essential feature of the work itself.
sentences.ja: この劇団にとって変化は同一公演の再現失敗でなく作品自体の不可欠な特徴である。

vocabulary.definition: having more than one possible meaning

questions.prompt: How does the audience experience the play?
options: By watching one fixed stage only.
By listening to one recording at home.

questions.prompt: Why will spectators understand events differently?
options: The actors tell entirely unrelated stories.
The director changes the building daily.
They encounter scenes in different orders.

questions.prompt: What concern does one actor raise?
options: Some spectators may miss essential information.
The theater has too many seats.
All audiences understand the ending identically.

questions.prompt: What distinction does the company make?
questions.explanation_ja: 有益な曖昧さと妨げる混乱。

options: To reveal all characters' motives directly.
To reduce practical obstacles unrelated to artistic interpretation.
questions.explanation_ja: 移動上の不要な混乱を減らす。

questions.prompt: What are spectators invited to do afterward?
Why might additional information fail to settle all disagreements?
options: Interpretations of intentions can still differ.
questions.explanation_ja: 意図の解釈は異なり得る。

options: Having more than one possible meaning.
Art can use varied encounters to reveal interpretation while reducing needless confusion.
All audiences must find one correct answer.
questions.explanation_ja: 多様な体験を芸術表現に生かす。

paraphrases.source: Because participants are unable to visit every room simultaneously, they encounter the scenes in different sequences.
paraphrases.rewrite: Spectators see scenes in different orders because they cannot be everywhere at once.

paraphrases.source: Another argues that missing information is an intentional feature of the performance rather than a problem that should automatically be eliminated.
paraphrases.rewrite: The actor views missing information as deliberate, not necessarily a defect.

paraphrases.source: She introduces recurring objects and phrases that connect separate rooms without explaining every relationship explicitly.
paraphrases.rewrite: Repeated elements link rooms while leaving some connections for viewers to infer.

paraphrases.source: For this theater company, variation is not a failure to reproduce an identical performance but an essential feature of the work itself.
paraphrases.rewrite: Variation belongs to the artwork itself rather than indicating failed reproduction.

discourse.role_ja: 実務的な改善と芸術性の両立。
